skeletal muscle activity and sudomotor activity are not necessarily dissociable during Pavlovian conditioning.
Dworkin and colleagues have demonstrated that skeletal motor activity does not mediate the vasomotor component of Pavlovian autonomic conditioning.
Dworkin and coworkers have not demonstrated a skeletal motor-autonomous dissociation, and that the tibial response of their study is most likely mediated by sudomotor processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autonomic responses are mediated by a wide variety of response mechanisms.
skeletal motor activity can be dissociated from sudomotor activity in the chronically denervated rat.
the autonomic nervous system is a more autonomous (independent of other systems) system than previously believed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vasomotion and sudomotion of the hind paw are controlled by different neural mechanisms.
the tibial response in Dworkin and colleagues’ work is not a skeletal motor response but is likely a sudomotor response.
the vasomotors are not a simple extension of the skeletal motoneurons.
